_readme: Demo dataset for the Round 2 prototype brief: 15-20 simulated patient records run through the real application (serve.py's own /api endpoints), plus a 3x surge replay. Every check_id below is a real CTAS discriminator id from triage/protocols/ctas.py. 'staff_observations' are posted via /api/observe -- the same endpoint a nurse uses to record a direct finding -- so the expected category is guaranteed regardless of which model tier (hosted / local / keyword-fallback) happens to be active during the run. 'narrative' and 'scripted_answers' still drive the real extraction -> VOI ranking -> choose_next() -> parse() pipeline end to end; their outcome is additional, never something the expected category depends on, matching the engine's own never-lowers-what-was-already-found rule.

patients.narrative: Pain in my upper stomach since this morning, feel sick and a bit sweaty.

staff_observations.note: on direct questioning, pain radiates up into the jaw

scripted_answers.pain_radiating: Yes, it goes up into my jaw a bit.

expected.rationale: pain_radiating fires Orange on the chest_pain branch even though the presenting complaint points at abdominal_pain
expected.notes: the flagship ambiguity case -- an inferior MI described as stomach pain

patients.narrative: Baby is having high fever since yesterday, very fussy and won't settle.

expected.rationale: fever_looks_unwell (Level 3) plus a moderate FLACC score
expected.notes: pre-verbal infant -- self-report pain questions are diverted to the FLACC observation, never asked directly

patients.narrative: Off his legs for two days, productive cough, generally unwell. On bisoprolol and apixaban.

staff_observations.note: mild increased work of breathing on exam

scripted_answers.resp_distress_mild: Yes, a little breathless when he moves around.

expected.rationale: resp_distress_mild (Level 3) -- the pulse and temperature read reassuring only because rate-limiting medication (from his record) makes them unreliable
expected.notes: the geriatric trap: normal-looking vitals in a patient who cannot mount the expected response

patients.narrative: Gestures to abdomen, visibly distressed. Minimal shared language, no ID.

staff_observations.note: gestured to abdomen, grimacing, scored 8/10 via interpreter gesture scale

expected.rationale: severe_pain_central confirmed directly, even though nothing else about this patient is known
expected.notes: low branch-attribution confidence is the CORRECT output here, not a failure -- decide() still acts on the one confirmed positive

patients.narrative: Sudden crushing chest pain, sweating, can't catch my breath.

scripted_answers.pain_radiating: Yes, into my left arm and jaw.
scripted_answers.cannot_complete_sentence: Yes, I can barely get a sentence out.

expected.rationale: spo2_under_90 and the compensated-shock rule (pulse over 120 with systolic under 100) both fire Red from vitals alone
expected.notes: the textbook case -- should_stop() should halt the interview the moment this lands

patients.narrative: Twisted my ankle playing five-a-side, hurts to walk on but I can put some weight on it.

expected.rationale: moderate peripheral pain, no high-risk mechanism
expected.notes: a plain, low-acuity walk-in -- the majority case the department actually sees

patients.narrative: Ate something with peanuts, lips swelling, feels like my throat is tightening.

staff_observations.note: visible lip and tongue swelling on exam

scripted_answers.throat_or_tongue_swelling: Yes, my throat feels like it's closing up.
scripted_answers.widespread_hives: Yes, hives all over my chest and arms.

expected.rationale: throat_or_tongue_swelling fires Orange on the allergic_reaction branch
expected.notes: airway involvement caught before it becomes shock/resp_distress_severe

patients.narrative: Sudden facial droop and slurred speech, family noticed twenty minutes ago.

staff_observations.note: facial droop, slurred speech, right arm weakness confirmed on exam

scripted_answers.new_neuro_deficit: Yes, my face feels droopy and my speech is slurred, it started suddenly.

expected.rationale: new_neuro_deficit fires Orange on the headache branch (FAST-positive, alert, no airway compromise)
expected.notes: geriatric, time-critical, but correctly Orange rather than Red -- there is no depressed consciousness here

patients.narrative: Two-year-old with a fever, off her food, mum says she's just not herself.

staff_observations.note: febrile, lethargic, not herself per mother

expected.notes: scored on the paediatric pathway, never the adult vital-sign chart

patients.narrative: Says she doesn't want to be here anymore, hasn't slept in days.

staff_observations.note: patient discloses active thoughts of self-harm on direct, sensitive questioning

expected.rationale: self_harm_risk fires Orange on the mental_health branch
expected.notes: Source.SENSITIVE -- never asked via the keyword tier, only ever recorded as a direct staff observation

patients.narrative: I'm 32 weeks pregnant and I'm bleeding, it's a lot.

staff_observations.note: 32 weeks gestation, heavy vaginal bleeding observed

scripted_answers.bleeding_third_trimester: 32 weeks, and it's soaking through quickly.

expected.rationale: bleeding_third_trimester is one of the two Level-1 second-order modifiers in the obstetric table (Sec 4.3.2)
expected.notes: the one branch in the pack where a second-order modifier outranks every first-order check except the shared resuscitation list

patients.narrative: Cut my hand on a kitchen knife, bleeding's stopped, probably needs stitches.

expected.rationale: moderate peripheral pain, no high-risk mechanism, not anticoagulated
expected.notes: exercises the record lookup for a patient with a prior history (asthma) that isn't relevant to this complaint

patients.narrative: Room spins when I turn my head, nothing else going on.

staff_observations.note: symptoms only with head movement, no other neuro signs on exam

scripted_answers.vertigo_positional_only: Yes, only when I move my head, nothing else.

expected.notes: isolated positional vertigo -- must stay below a case with any neuro deficit

patients.narrative: Feeling dizzy, haven't eaten anything since morning.

scripted_answers.vertigo_positional_only: No, it's not really related to moving my head, just feel light-headed generally.

expected.rationale: nothing confirmed positive -- low blood sugar from not eating, no danger signal on any branch
expected.notes: the original real case that started this whole investigation -- landing quickly on the right (low) category with no irrelevant questions in between, now that the cubed VOI discount and choose_next() are in place

patients.narrative: Mild headache since this morning, nothing else.

expected.notes: the interim read, before the deterioration below is applied

deterioration.note: simulates a nurse re-assessment finding a new deficit a short time after arrival

staff_observations.note: new right-sided weakness noted on reassessment

expected.rationale: new_neuro_deficit fires Orange on the headache branch -- the initial score is never overwritten, this is a fresh, appended finding
expected.notes: demonstrates the reassessment path, not just the first-contact score

patients.narrative: Child has a rash that isn't going away, feels really unwell.

staff_observations.note: rash does not fade under glass test -- non-blanching
cool peripheries, prolonged capillary refill, tachycardic on exam

expected.rationale: shock is a shared first-order Level-1 check (age-agnostic -- direct clinical observation, not a numeric monitor threshold, so it is not withheld by the paediatric adult-threshold gate); non_blanching_rash alone would only fire Orange on the rash branch
expected.notes: third Red case, and a reminder that non_blanching_rash by itself is Orange, not Red -- the septic-shock finding is what makes this one Red

patients.narrative: Just some mild stomach upset since last night, nothing major.

expected.notes: another low-acuity baseline case for the case-mix spread

patients.narrative: Passed out for a few seconds while running, came round quickly, feel fine now.

scripted_answers.syncope_exertional: Yes, I was running when it happened.

expected.rationale: syncope_exertional fires Orange on the collapse branch -- exertional syncope is a recognised cardiac-cause marker
expected.notes: a 'feels fine now' patient whose true acuity would be missed by triaging on symptoms present at that moment alone
